title: SRE handoff + incident digest (week of 2026-07-22)
content:
Week summary

Owners: Alex Kim (primary), Priya Shah (secondary)
On-call rotation: Week B (Diego -> Samira shadow)

Overview:
This doc captures the on-call handoff notes for the week, the two notable incidents we handled (both short but instructive), SLO status and error-budget accounting, runbook updates we made, and action items for the next on-call cycle. Intended audience: SREs, platform eng, and any on-call engineers who might take the next rotation.

Key incidents this week

1) Incident: Edge proxy TLS handshake failures (2026-07-23 03:40 - 04:05 UTC)
- Severity: SEV2 (brief customer impact to hosted inference requests hitting EU region)
- Impact: ~2.4% of requests returned 500/502 during peak minute window. Visible in dashboards: proxy-502-rate spike in eu-west-1. Affected customers saw short-lived request failures; retries recovered most requests.
- Detection: Alert triggered by proxy-502-rate > 0.5% for 3 min (pager fired at 03:43).
- Root cause hypothesis: Certificate rotation job (internal cert-rotator) updated a subset of proxy instances earlier than rolling health-checks completed; the new certs were valid but intermediate CA missing on a subset of OS images (older base image). Handshake failed intermittently with clients that validated the full chain.
- Timeline summary:
  - 03:40 Alert fired (metrics).
  - 03:43 Primary on-call acknowledged and paged Diego.
  - 03:45 Confirmed 502s correlated with cert-rotator job logs.
  - 03:50 Rolled back cert-rotator change via feature flag; started rolling restart for affected proxy fleet to pick up older cert bundle.
  - 04:02 Metrics returned to baseline; incident closed at 04:05 after 30m observation.
- Mitigation steps taken:
  - Feature-flagged the cert-rotator to use the fallback CA bundle.
  - Manually restarted the 4 affected proxy pods (k8s) with older base image.
  - Opened emergency PR to add intermediate CA into the cert-rotator config. (PR: linked above)
- Post-mortem status: Draft RCA created (JIRA SRE-4123). Next steps are to harden cert-rotator preflight checks and add an integration test that verifies full chain validation on representative base images.
- Notes for next on-call: Check cert-rotator runbook section and validate cert chain on canary images before rollout.

2) Incident: KV-cache eviction spike affecting latency-sensitive model requests (2026-07-24 11:12 - 11:45 UTC)
- Severity: SEV3 (increased tail latency, no customer-visible errors)
- Impact: p99 latency for hosted text-generation rose from 460ms -> 1.1s for ~30 minutes for small-batch traffic. No 5xxs, but timeouts increased for some interactive demos.
- Detection: Observability alert for p99 latency > 800ms for 5m.
- Root cause hypothesis: Autoscaler for the model-serving layer applied an aggressive mem-pressure eviction policy after a background memory leak in an older model variant triggered temporary cache pressure. Continuous batching caused more cache thrash than expected under this policy.
- Timeline summary:
  - 11:12 Alert fired and on-call acknowledged at 11:15.
  - 11:18 Identified elevated mem-eviction events in model-serving logs.
  - 11:25 Scaled up dedicated pool by +2 nodes (temporary) to increase aggregate cache capacity.
  - 11:35 Deployed a mitigative configuration: relaxed eviction aggressiveness and enabled stash-mode for long-tail KV entries.
  - 11:45 p99 latency returned to baseline.
- Mitigation steps taken:
  - Throttled background job frequency that was leaking memory.
  - Scaled up pool and adjusted eviction thresholds temporarily.
  - Added logging around cache eviction reasons for future diagnostics.
- Follow-ups: SRE-4178 opened to track the memory leak root cause in background job; implement a cache-metric-based autoscaling policy rather than raw mem pressure.
- Notes for next on-call: If mem eviction increases, scale up pool earlier (runbook patch updated below).

SLO and error budget snapshot (end of week)
- Availability SLO (hosted API - global): 99.90% monthly target. This week: 99.96% (no burn).
- Latency SLO (generation p95 global): 600ms target. This week: p95 = 520ms (healthy).
- Error budget burn: The TLS incident consumed ~0.01% of monthly budget; we remain well within budget.
- Noted trend: Small upward drift in p99 tail latency for low-traffic demo buckets correlated with KV-cache eviction pattern. Action item to add per-customer tail sampling.

Runbook updates made this week
- Added a section to "cert-rotator" runbook: preflight validation to verify intermediate CA chain presence on all supported base images; added sample openssl command and expected output.
- Updated model-serving autoscaler runbook: temporary scale-up recommendation when p99 > 800ms AND mem-evictions > 10/min. Added a checklist prompt to contact solutions-eng when dedicated pools are scaled for >2 hours.
- Documented a short troubleshooting checklist for intermittent 502s that includes: check cert-rotator logs, check proxy image baseline, check client validation flags.

Operational changes and decisions
- Short term: Disable auto-rotation of intermediate CA bundles until integration test added (owners: Priya, due 2026-08-05).
- Medium term: Replace mem-pressure-only autoscaling with cache-aware policy; prototyping tracked in SRE-4178 (owner: Diego, due 2026-09-01).
- Observability: Add new Grafana dashboard panel for 'kv-cache-evictions per node' (owner: Samira, due 2026-07-30).

Handoff notes for next on-call (week starting 2026-07-25)
- Primary concerns for next week: cert-rotator integration tests not yet merged; there is a small possibility of a repeat if a patch rolls out. Watch proxy-502-rate and cert-rotator job runs.
- Key runbooks to review: cert-rotator, model-serving-autoscaler, edge-proxy-failover. Links in linked_artifacts.
- Slack channels: #sre-oncall, #infra-deploys, #hosted-api-ops. If any certificate rotation job is scheduled, coordinate with Priya and tag the run in Slack at least 24 hours prior.
- Scheduled changes to note next week: planned model-serving pool upgrade on 2026-07-28 02:00 UTC (low risk) — keep an eye on autoscaler behavior post-upgrade.

Action items and owners (short list)
- Priya Shah: Add intermediate CA to cert-rotator config and create automated preflight check (due 2026-08-05).
- Diego Ramirez: Investigate background job memory leak and deliver a mitigation plan (SRE-4178) (due 2026-08-12).
- Samira Patel: Add kv-cache-evictions panel to Grafana and set an alert for >50 evictions/min/node (due 2026-07-30).
- Alex Kim: Draft post-incident blameless RCA for TLS incident and schedule async review with infra and security (due 2026-07-30).

Meeting notes (standup snippets)
- Mon 07/22 standup: Discussed TLS alerting granularity; proposal to split proxy-5xx alert into TLS-specific and backend-error-specific streams. Action: draft alert change (Alex).
- Tue 07/23 incident war-room: Kept communication concise. Suggestion from solutions-eng to add client-side fallback to alternate endpoint when 502 rates exceed threshold. Added to backlog.
- Thu 07/24 retro: Agreed that cache-aware autoscaling is higher priority than tuning eviction thresholds alone.

Troubleshooting snippets / useful commands
- Check cert chain on node: openssl s_client -showcerts -connect localhost:443 | sed -n '/-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----/,/-----END CERTIFICATE-----/p'
- Kubernetes restart for proxy pod: kubectl rollout restart deployment/edge-proxy -n infra --context=eu-west-1
- Quick mem-eviction probe: kubectl logs -l app=model-serving -n model --tail=200 | grep -i eviction | wc -l

Appendix: quick metrics snapshot (approx)
- proxy-502-rate peak minute: 2.4% (03:44 UTC 07/23)
- hosted-api p99 pre-incident: 460ms, during eviction spike: 1.1s, post-mitigation: 480ms
- kv-cache evictions: peaked at 72 evictions/min/node during spike

Notes to self / informal
- Remember: rotate test can catch chain problems on older base images — our fleet still runs a few historical images for customers on dedicated pools.
- Put an item on the infra office-hours agenda next week to discuss test coverage for cert rotation.

If you pick up on-call: ack the #sre-oncall pinned message, run the quick health checks linked above, and skim the two open JIRAs (SRE-4123, SRE-4178). Reach out to Priya or Diego if you need context.

End of digest.
